turn.question: My laptop screen started flickering. Am I still covered?
turn.question_sent: My laptop screen started flickering. Am I still covered?
turn.answer:
**Covered:** Yes. The warranty is valid until 03/01/2027 (“*Warranty valid until: 03/01/2027*”). Since today (30 Oct 2026) is on or before that date and the screen‑flickering fault is not listed among the exclusions (exclusions are accidental damage, liquid spills, and cosmetic damage), the issue is likely covered.

**Steps to claim:**
1. Back up any important data on the laptop.  
2. Locate your receipt/invoice [ACCOUNT_1] and note the service tag [SERIAL_1].  
3. Visit Dell’s official support page for warranty claims:  
   - https://www.dell.com/support/kbdoc/en-us/000132371/how-to-create-a-support-request-online-for-dell-emc  
   - https://www.dell.com/support/home/en-us  
4. Follow the online instructions to create a support request, providing the product details, purchase date, invoice number, service tag, and a description of the screen‑flickering fault.  
5. Alternatively, you can use the draft email below to contact Dell (they will usually direct you to the support site).

**Links from search:**  
- https://www.dell.com/support/kbdoc/en-us/000132371/how-to-create-a-support-request-online-for-dell-emc  
- https://www.dell.com/support/home/en-us  

**Draft ready:** A draft email to Dell has been saved (draft ID draft-5b1477). Review it in the app, edit if needed, and send it yourself (or submit the claim via the support site).  

*Remember:* Always back up your data before sending the device in for repair. If you need further assistance, let me know.

args.title: Warranty Claim – Dell XPS 13
args.body:
Dear Dell Support,

I am writing to request warranty service for my Dell XPS 13 laptop (Service Tag: [SERIAL_1]). The laptop was purchased on 03/01/2026 (invoice [ACCOUNT_1]) from Northwind Electronics and is currently experiencing screen flickering.

Under the one‑year limited hardware warranty (valid until 03/01/2027), I believe this issue is covered as a hardware defect. Please advise on the next steps for repair or replacement.

Thank you,
[PERSON_1]
